title: pipeline-guardrails
description: Machine-readable rules for the partner pipeline. Phase 1 authoring artifact. This file documents intent; it is NOT a running enforcement mechanism. Technical enforcement (hooks, permissions) is designed and tested separately in a later phase.

git_identity.method: per-command environment variables; never modify global git config

coordinator.who: main conversation Claude session (NOT a subagent, no coordinator.md file)
responsibilities: clarify objective with Laura when ambiguous
classify risk before any subagent runs; any doubt escalates one tier
build each subagent's isolated input slice
validate every handoff against handoff.schema.json before forwarding
validate every artifact: valid JSON, required fields, valid enums
stop pipeline (BLOCKED) on insufficient data and state exactly what is missing
archive without notifying Laura only: IGNORE, MONITOR meeting all archive conditions, minor/duplicate/irrelevant
present to Laura only the cases in laura_notify_when, as the 8-point brief
produce a coordinator-decision artifact per run
must_not: extend a Laura approval by interpretation
auto-archive anything whose next step is merge/push/deploy/publish/external/spend/live change
send Telegram or email in Phase 1 (relay to Laura in the conversation instead)

read_only_zero_write.rule: These five stages make ZERO writes anywhere: not the official repo, not the sandbox, not the isolated temporary test repo, not OS temp (%TEMP%/%TMP%/$TMPDIR//tmp or any other OS temp location), not via a helper script, and not as the side effect of a cache- or artifact-producing command. A write under OS temp is NOT non-blocking - it is the same violation as any other.
forbidden_vectors: Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit tool use
shell output redirection to a file (>, >>, 2>file)
pipe to a file-writing command (| tee, | Out-File, | Set-Content)
heredoc or here-string file creation (<<EOF ... EOF, @'...'@, @"..."@)
Set-Content, Add-Content, Out-File, New-Item, Export-Csv, Export-Clixml
copy/move/delete: cp, mv, rm, cp/copy, move, del, Remove-Item, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Rename-Item, mkdir
any write into OS temp, including via mktemp/mkdtemp/GetTempFileName
read_only_zero_write.who_may_write_instead: Only the Implementer, and only inside the isolated temporary test repo created outside the official repo (unchanged) -- PLUS, as of QA_VERIFIER_SCOPE_AND_REPRODUCTION_FIX, QA may create EPHEMERAL_VERIFICATION_ARTIFACTS under the narrow exception below; QA still writes nowhere else. The Coordinator/harness may create the sandbox, run artifacts, and logs - that is a harness write, never a subagent write, and the two are never conflated in a report.
read_only_zero_write.on_violation: the run is a deterministic test FAIL, the pipeline is BLOCKED, and the offending stage's artifact is NOT forwarded to the next stage
read_only_zero_write.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in each read-only agent's .md ('Zero-write contract' section) + in TESTPLAN.md, and checked statically by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-agent-writes.mjs (frontmatter tool grants, contract text presence, and a positive/negative detector battery over synthetic tool-call records; --events-dir=<run-dir> scans real per-stage tool-event logs during a behavioral run). Hook / permission enforcement is a later phase.

qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exce.rule: QA -- and only QA -- may create an EPHEMERAL_VERIFICATION_ARTIFACT (e.g. a throwaway synthetic scratch DB) to independently reproduce a technical invariant a read-only check cannot confirm, strictly outside every repo/worktree, and ONLY when all ten conditions in qa.md's 'EPHEMERAL_VERIFICATION_ARTIFACTS' section hold: (1) isolated temp/scratch location only; (2) never inside the official repo, sandbox, isolated temp test repo, or any verification_scope repo/worktree; (3) never modifies the source under verification; (4) never real data/PII; (5) synthetic/fixture input only; (6) exists exclusively to run/reproduce one test; (7) removed after the test wherever the mechanism supports it; (8) any reported path is secret-free; (9) any write attempt inside a target/declared repo or worktree is STILL an absolute FAIL under the unmodified zero-write rule -- this exception widens nothing about that; (10) production/live data is completely out of reach.
qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exce.schema: handoff.schema.json -> qaReport.ephemeral_scratch (optional object; target_repo_modified is schema-const false -- a truthful report of a repo write cannot even validate against this branch)
qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exce.does_not_widen: the read_only_zero_write rule above for the other four roles, or QA's own prohibition on repo/worktree writes -- this is a scratch-creation exception only, never a fix/merge/push/deploy exception, and it is not a general write grant

strict_json_output.rule: Every agent reply is EXACTLY one JSON object: first character '{', last character '}', no preamble, no trailing text, no second object, no Markdown of any kind, no code fence, no ` ```json ` wrapper, no bare word 'json' anywhere in the reply, no backtick character anywhere in the reply, no repeated/restated schema, no worked examples, and no artificial HTML-escaping of <, >, or & in any string value. Every explanation goes in an approved schema field, never outside the object. This rule is stated twice in each agent's .md: immediately before the field-by-field output contract, and again as the literal last section of the file ('Final output rule (read this last...)'), ending with a 5-step self-check (check first/last character; check exactly one object; check no backticks; check against schema; only then return it).
strict_json_output.comparison_notation_guidance: root-caused from the SMK-ANA RETRY_EXHAUSTED incident, 2026-08-31: a reproducer (an unrelated generic agent, given an explicit, trivial, verbatim-copy instruction including 'do not HTML-escape') still returned ASCII < > & HTML-entity-encoded 100% of the time, while Unicode equivalents (≥ ≤), word form ('at least', 'no more than'), em/en dashes, and quotes all passed through unescaped. This proves the escaping is a systemic platform/transport behavior between agent generation and the Coordinator's view of the reply, not an Analyst-specific or test_plan-specific defect, and not fixable by re-instruction (the existing 'do not HTML-escape' rule above was already present verbatim and still failed 3 consecutive attempts). A first, narrower fix (comparison/threshold/range language only) was validated clean on the original success_threshold/stop_threshold fields, but the SAME post-fix validation run immediately surfaced a second, related instance in a DIFFERENT field (test_plan.change: the Analyst wrote the literal HTML tag name '<title>', which was escaped to '<title>') - proving the platform behavior is not scoped to comparisons, so the guidance was broadened to any freshly-composed prose that would otherwise need a literal <, >, or &, covering at minimum (1) comparisons/thresholds/ranges and (2) HTML/XML tag-name references ('the title tag', never '<title>'). Per CLAUDE.md's layer model this is a genuine technical-control gap, not something to route around by weakening the checker: the STRICT-JSON-GATE escaping check is NOT relaxed and MUST NOT normalize >/</& back to literals. This is a notation choice, not a rule relaxation: a literal <, >, or & already present in a value being copied from the input must still be reproduced as the literal character per the rule above. UPDATE, F-9c, 2026-08-31: the previously-flagged open risk (no fixture at the time contained a literal <, >, or & requiring verbatim reproduction) has now been demonstrated for real: FX-03/F-0003's own 'Deterministic success criterion' text contains literal '<h1>', and a real E2E-LOW QA run copied it verbatim into success_criteria per the letter of the rule above, which the platform then encoded to '<h1>', tripping check-json-output.mjs's escaping scan even though the agent never deviated from its input. Root cause: 'reproduce literal input verbatim' and 'the platform escapes ANY agent-authored <, >, & regardless of provenance or intent' are in direct, unavoidable conflict for this one narrow shape - a tag-name reference sitting inside an otherwise-verbatim natural-language sentence. Fix: carved out specifically - and ONLY - a tag-name reference in that position is retold in word form ('the h1 element') even while transcribing verbatim, since the tag name itself carries no test-critical information a word-form retelling doesn't equally carry; an exact expected string or a literal href inside the same sentence is still never paraphrased. No other verbatim-reproduction case is touched by this carve-out. Checked statically by check-json-output.mjs's tagNameCarveOut flag.
strict_json_output.on_violation: the reply is rejected BEFORE handoff, is not forwarded to the next stage, and the run is FAIL — the harness does not clean up or reformat a non-conforming reply
strict_json_output.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in each agent's .md ('Output format (strict)' section placed before the contract, and the 'Final output rule' section placed last), and checked statically by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-json-output.mjs (contract text presence including the first/last-character, comparison-notation, and final-self-check language + a positive/negative parser battery: single object, fenced, prose-before, prose-after, two-objects, any backtick anywhere, unjustified-HTML-escaping; --file=<reply> validates one real reply); reissue-scope integrity (a retry changes only the field(s) named by the validator error) is checked by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-retry-policy.mjs -> checkRetryScopeIntegrity().

format_retry_policy.trigger: ONLY a format/parse failure (STRICT-JSON-GATE, check-json-output.mjs) or a schema-validation failure (handoff.schema.json) on the agent's raw reply. NEVER a semantic disagreement, a qa.overall == FAIL, a verifier.overall the Coordinator would prefer different, a verifier.overall that disagrees with the Decision Engine's independently computed verdict (roles.verifier.decision_table), or any other outcome the Coordinator dislikes - those route back through the normal flow (see roles/decision tables), they are not retried as if they were a format problem.

on_reject.label: REJECTED_FORMAT (fails STRICT-JSON-GATE) or REJECTED_SCHEMA (parses but fails handoff.schema.json)
on_reject.archive_retention: kept even after a later attempt succeeds - never overwritten or dropped from the report

must_include: the identical isolated input from the failed attempt, byte-for-byte
the exact validator error text from the failed attempt
an instruction to re-emit the artifact correcting only that defect
must_not_include: any hint at the expected verdict, value, or decision
any summary of what was 'wrong' beyond the literal validator error

on_exhaustion.condition: attempt_1 AND retry_1 AND retry_2 all fail format/schema validation
on_exhaustion.laura_told: exactly which stage and which validator error recurred three times
forbidden_next_steps: manual repair of the reply by the Coordinator

on_recovery.condition: attempt_1, or retry_1, or retry_2 validates (strict JSON + schema)
on_recovery.never_hides: the count and raw content of the invalid attempt(s)

never_do_on_a_rejected_reply: strip a trailing comma and accept it
strip a Markdown fence and accept it
extract the JSON object from surrounding prose and accept it
run it through a tolerant/lenient parser
forward it to the next stage under any circumstance

verifier_determinism_interaction.rule: ISO-VER (TESTPLAN.md sec. D) compares only the FIRST VALID artifact of each of the three independent runs. A rejected attempt is excluded from the comparison and may be reissued per this protocol, but the reissue never carries the desired verdict - it receives only the structural/format/schema error, never a semantic hint.
verifier_determinism_interaction.on_disagreement: if the first valid artifacts of the three independent runs disagree on overall, the test stays FAIL - the retry protocol never turns semantic non-determinism into a passing result

format_retry_policy.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in CLAUDE.md sec. 7 + README.md sec. 2a + TESTPLAN.md (RETRY-GATE, Acceptance sec. G) + a short 'Format-retry reissue' note in each agent's .md, and checked statically by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-retry-policy.mjs (contract text presence in this file and in each agent's .md, plus a pure-function battery: format-reject-then-recover -> PASS_RECOVERED, schema-reject-then-recover -> PASS_RECOVERED, three consecutive rejects -> BLOCKED, a clean first attempt -> PASS, an invalid attempt never appears in the forwarded/handoff set, and the reissue-prompt builder never includes a semantic hint or expected-verdict field).

schema_keywords_are_not_artifact_fields.rule: These are JSON Schema vocabulary, not artifact fields. No agent ever copies one into its output as a top-level key. Every artifact branch is additionalProperties:false, so an injected schema-keyword key is rejected as an unexpected key before handoff, the same as any other extra key.
schema_keywords_are_not_artifact_fields.documented_in: each agent's .md, inside the 'Output format (strict)' section, immediately before the field-by-field contract
schema_keywords_are_not_artifact_fields.enforcement_status_phase1: check-fixtures.mjs section 3 rejects any top-level key not in the schema branch's properties (this already covers the seven schema-keyword words); agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-schema-key-negtest.mjs proves it by injecting each of the seven words as a top-level key into a real artifact fixture copy and asserting check-fixtures.mjs names every one as an unexpected key.

competitor-intelligence.input: a public-source monitoring target (query, location, competitor id) from the Coordinator
competitor-intelligence.output: competitor-observation artifact(s), 15 fields, certainty in {OBSERVED, ESTIMATED, UNVERIFIED} - never CONFIRMED
allowed_operations: fetch public web pages, robots.txt, sitemaps
read Ads Transparency Center public data
read public business directories and public social pages
read PSS own monitor history (agent/state/keyword-rankings.json) and PSS own exports
forbidden_operations: log in to any competitor system
copy competitor text, images, or branding
produce recommendations, preferred solutions, causal claims, or budget/conversion/revenue assumptions
stop_conditions: a source requires login or CAPTCHA
cannot establish source URL and timestamp for an observation
would need to assert a non-public fact

investigator.input: a raw finding: competitor-observation, an L1 check issue, or an opportunity-backlog item id - facts only
investigator.output: investigation artifact with atomic_claims + evidence_ledger; observed_facts and estimates kept separate
allowed_operations: open and read the cited sources independently
forbidden_operations: use ARCHIVE_MINOR for a finding that is not a confirmed duplicate (route non-duplicate low-impact findings TO_ANALYST)
stop_conditions: claims cannot be made atomic with evidence
the finding is a CONFIRMED DUPLICATE of an already-resolved item -> recommended_next = ARCHIVE_MINOR (the only use of ARCHIVE_MINOR)
a required file is outside the fixture allow-list in a fixture-only test run -> BLOCKED

analyst.output: analysis artifact incl. decision in {IGNORE, MONITOR, INVESTIGATE_FURTHER, PROPOSE_TEST, URGENT_RISK}, risk_class, and a separate test_plan object
allowed_operations: assess business relevance against PSS metric priority
design an ORIGINAL minimal test with KPI/risk/duration/rollback
forbidden_operations: verify its own facts (that is the Verifier's job)
copy competitor text, images, or branding into the proposal
stop_conditions: facts are insufficient to assess relevance -> decision = INVESTIGATE_FURTHER
no legal/feasible PSS action exists -> decision = IGNORE or MONITOR

verifier.output: verification artifact with overall in {CONFIRMED, REFUTED, INSUFFICIENT_DATA} and context_leak_detected flag
checks: does the opportunity follow logically from the fact
can PSS implement this legally and technically
does the test measure the stated hypothesis

a public_evidence entry with source_type qa_reproduction_evidence is evaluated exactly like any other entry (reproduction-boundary rule unchanged) and may serve as TESTED corroboration for the alternative it bears on -- see verifier_reverification_with_qa_corroboration; this adds no tool, no capability, and no exception to the Verifier's zero-write / zero-independent-gathering contract

alternative_explanations_contract.note: ISO-VER-1 fix: the free boolean alternative_explanations_reviewed is retired. The Verifier instead emits a structured alternative_explanations array (schema: handoff.schema.json -> verification.alternative_explanations); each entry carries alternative_id, description, applicability (APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE), verification_status (TESTED/NOT_TESTED/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), evidence_ids, reason, required_control, control_result (PASS/FAIL/INSUFFICIENT/NOT_APPLICABLE).
alternative_explanations_contract.mandatory_set_is_deterministic: the set of required alternative_id entries is a pure function of test_plan/input, documented in verifier.md ('Deriving the mandatory alternative-explanations list') and mirrored by check-verifier-decision-table.mjs -> deriveMandatoryAlternativeIds() (a reference/self-tested function only - it is never called by computeOfficialVerdict() or checkHandoff() and is not on the live Decision Engine path); it is never invented freely per run, and differing description/reason wording across runs never changes the verdict, only the structured fields do
alternative_explanations_contract.background_only_claim_scoping: F-11c fix, root-caused from a real ISO-VER-1/FX-09 run, 2026-08-31: the derivation rule for ALT-1 (seasonality)/ALT-2 (concurrent deploy) asks whether ANY claim has a time dimension or deploy/control signal; a real Verifier run applied this to a claim the input itself explicitly marks background-only (not the opportunity under verification), forcing overall to INSUFFICIENT_DATA on a fixture designed to resolve CONFIRMED. Fix (verifier.md, 'Deriving the mandatory alternative-explanations list' -> scoping step): rules 1-2 apply only to decision-relevant claims/evidence - ones the test_plan.hypothesis is actually about - excluding any claim or public_evidence entry whose own text already marks it background-only (the same 'background context only' / 'not the opportunity under verification' language rule 4 already treats as a scope boundary, extended from rule 4 to also govern rules 1-2's applicability trigger). The marker must already be present in substance in the given input text - the Verifier never invents it unprompted, which keeps the scoping step itself deterministic. ALT-3 (measurement/tracking artifact) is NOT scoped by this rule, since a tracking artifact can affect any measured number regardless of decision-relevance. This is a Verifier-contract-only fix: computeOfficialVerdict(), checkHandoff(), and validateAlternativeExplanations() in check-verifier-decision-table.mjs are unchanged - the Decision Engine still reads only the Verifier's own reported applicability/verification_status/control_result fields, and remains the sole, deterministic, unmodified authority over overall. Regression battery: check-verifier-decision-table.mjs section 8b.
alternative_explanations_contract.background_only_extends_to_coupled_contr: F-11d fix, root-caused from a live 3x ISO-VER-1/FX-09 rerun after F-11c landed, 2026-08-31: even with F-11c applied, 1 of 3 real Verifier runs still classified ALT-1/ALT-2 as APPLICABLE (citing the deploy-control evidence, e.g. FX-09's EV-0004/C-004) while the other 2 correctly classified them NOT_APPLICABLE - a genuine classification split the ISO-VER-1 determinism fix exists to catch, even though all 3 runs still agreed on the same final overall (driven independently by the always-mandatory ALT-3 and by a rule-4 confound named in that same evidence entry's own limitations). Root cause: the scoping step told the Verifier to check whether a CLAIM is marked background-only, but did not say what to do when a public_evidence entry is not itself that claim's evidence, yet exists only to explain/control for it (e.g. a control-page comparison whose own method/limitations text is entirely about ruling out causes of an already-background-only decline). Fix (verifier.md scoping step, same paragraph as F-11c): such a coupled control-evidence entry is scoped as part of the same background-only story for ALT-1/ALT-2 triggering purposes, even though it can still independently earn its own ALT-n under rule 4 from its own limitations text (rule 4 is unaffected). No Decision Engine change. Not re-validated by a 4th empirical ISO-VER-1 rerun in this session (2 of the 3 already-collected runs already exhibit the corrected behavior); the literal ISO-VER-1 acceptance gate (fixtures/expected/assertions.json) never required a specific overall value, only same-verdict-on-all-3-runs plus per-run self-consistency plus structural validity, all of which held before and after this fix.
artifact_validity_rules: a TESTED entry with empty evidence_ids is an invalid artifact (rejected before the Decision Engine computes a verdict)
a NOT_APPLICABLE entry with a placeholder reason (n/a, none, not applicable, or similarly empty of content) is an invalid artifact
duplicate or missing alternative_id values make the artifact invalid
alternative_explanations_contract.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in verifier.md + in handoff.schema.json's field description, and checked by check-verifier-decision-table.mjs -> validateAlternativeExplanations()

decision_table.note: overall is the Verifier's own SELF-CHECK reading of the rule below -- informative only. The OFFICIAL verdict is computed independently by the Coordinator's Decision Engine (check-verifier-decision-table.mjs -> computeOfficialVerdict()) from the atomic fields listed in mandatory_controls plus alternative_explanations, never from the Verifier's own overall value. If the Verifier's overall disagrees with the Decision Engine's recomputation, the artifact is rejected before handoff -- not corrected, not forwarded. No agent (Coordinator included) may override the computed verdict. The same input always yields the same computed verdict; full rule in verifier.md ('Decision Engine').
decision_table.authority: the Decision Engine script, not the Verifier and not the Coordinator, is authoritative for overall
order: 3. else any mandatory control INSUFFICIENT (or data_sufficient == FAIL), or any APPLICABLE alternative_explanations entry has verification_status in {NOT_TESTED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE} or control_result == INSUFFICIENT -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA

4. else any remaining mandatory control FAIL (opportunity_follows_logically / pss_can_implement_legally_and_technically / test_measures_hypothesis), or any APPLICABLE alternative_explanations entry has control_result == FAIL -> REFUTED
5. else all mandatory controls PASS and every APPLICABLE alternative_explanations entry is PASS or a justified NOT_APPLICABLE -> CONFIRMED
decision_table.non_fatal: declared limitations and contested_points never move overall off the table's result once every mandatory control is PASS
decision_table.verifier_overall_vs_official_verdict: the artifact's own overall field is the Verifier's self-check and is retained for continuity (HO-4 etc. still read it), but check-verifier-decision-table.mjs -> checkHandoff() never treats it as authoritative -- disagreement with the recomputed value is a handoff-blocking condition (VERIFIER-TABLE-GATE), not a format/schema issue and NOT eligible for format_retry_policy

stop_conditions: input contains reasoning/persuasion -> set context_leak_detected = true and overall = INSUFFICIENT_DATA
a claimed fact cannot be independently reproduced -> overall = REFUTED or INSUFFICIENT_DATA

implementer.input: a verified finding + the approved change scope (in RIDICAT, only after LAURA APPROVAL 1)
implementer.output: implementation artifact; work committed on a branch in the isolated temp test repo
allowed_tools: Bash(git local in temp repo + node --check)
allowed_operations: commit on a branch in the temp test repo
forbidden_operations: write, branch, commit, or stash in the official PSS repo
widen the change beyond the prescribed scope
stop_conditions: the prescribed change would touch more than the approved files
the change cannot be made minimal or reversible
any step would require writing to the official repo or an external service

qa.input: an implementation artifact + the success criteria + optional verification_scope
qa.output: qa-report artifact with overall in {PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED}
qa.writes_any_file: false, except an EPHEMERAL_VERIFICATION_ARTIFACT under qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exception (never inside any repo/worktree)
checks: temp repo delta matches the prescribed delta exactly
target repo (verification_scope.target_repo, or the one implicit target when verification_scope is absent) is byte-identical to its baseline (hash + clean status)
each declared verification_scope dependency/expected-unchanged repo is UNCHANGED (external_repo_checks) -- a repo NOT declared in verification_scope is out of scope and never checked or blamed
optionally: independent reproduction of a technical invariant in ephemeral synthetic scratch, reported as reproduction_evidence, when asked under verifier_reverification_with_qa_corroboration
forbidden_operations: write inside the target repo or any declared dependency repo/worktree, ever, under any exception
use real data or PII in any ephemeral verification artifact
decide an alternative_explanations verdict (that stays the Verifier's job)
stop_conditions: target repo differs from baseline -> overall = FAIL, blocking_reasons records it
a declared dependency/expected-unchanged repo shows CHANGED_UNEXPECTED -> overall = FAIL
success criteria are not deterministic -> overall = BLOCKED
an ephemeral-verification-artifact request cannot meet all ten qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exception conditions -> do not create it; BLOCKED or FAIL/note naming the failed condition

all_conditions_required: no bulk scripts / no multi-page generated output

handoff_order: analysis(atomic_claims + public_evidence + pss_data + period_filters + test_plan only) -> verification
laura_notify_when: verified opportunity with relevant business impact
pipeline BLOCKED for lack of information
approval required before implementation or a live operation

archive_without_notifying_laura.MONITOR: only if ALL: low impact AND no urgent risk AND no near-term deadline AND no cost AND no external operation AND review_date set
archive_without_notifying_laura.READY_FOR_MERGE: NOT an archive class - a QA PASS alone never authorizes merge/push/deploy/publish/external/spend/live change; escalate with human_review_state instead

isolation.runs_and_logs: created OUTSIDE the official repo (session scratchpad); never committed; .gitignore is NOT modified for them
isolation.test_repo: a throwaway `git init` repo + a bare `../testrepo-remote.git` origin, both outside the official repo; fictional data only; no credentials; no external access; deleted after each test

fixture_only_test_mode.applies_to: every ACCEPTANCE and EXTENDED suite run, and any run whose input is a fixture under agent/workflow/pipeline/fixtures/
fixture_only_test_mode.purpose: make offline tests hermetic - an agent under test reasons only from static fixture copies in a sandbox, never from the live official repo, secrets, real PSS commercial data, or the network
fixture_only_test_mode.not_a_permission_change: scoped to test runs only; it does NOT narrow the Investigator's or any agent's authorised read-only access to the official repo in a real, non-test task
coordinator_builds: an allow-list manifest (agent/workflow/pipeline/fixtures/fixture-manifest.json) naming every fixture file a run may use, each with its sha256

the full sandbox inventory (agent/workflow/pipeline/fixtures/sandbox-manifest.json) naming every file the sandbox may hold - the 18 fixtures plus the 2 structural-contract schemas - each with its sandbox path, category, allowed roles, and sha256
a sandbox directory OUTSIDE the official repo holding EXACTLY the files declared in sandbox-manifest.json - no more, no fewer - verified by sha256 after copy
each agent input slice built ONLY from the sandbox entries whose roles list names that agent; an entry with roles:[] never enters any agent slice
each agent input slice that references only sandbox paths and fixture:// identifiers
agent_rules: read only files that are inside the sandbox AND listed in the manifest
treat every fixture:// identifier as data already embedded in the input - never resolve it against the official repo or the network
no read of the official repo working tree, .git, .env or .env.local, token or OAuth files, agent/state, agent/google-ads, agent/gsc-snapshots, or any real PSS export
no network - no WebFetch, no curl, no fetch - the fixtures carry all evidence inline

for the five read-only roles (competitor-intelligence, investigator, analyst, verifier, qa): ZERO tool use of any kind in fixture-only-test mode - not Read, not Grep, not Glob, not Bash, not WebFetch, not WebSearch, not even a read-only call; tool_uses must be exactly 0; everything needed is inline in the input; a sandbox path in the input is for the Coordinator's audit trail only, never an invitation to read it

auto-loaded context is not an exception: a subagent's context may already contain project/system content injected before the input arrived (e.g. CLAUDE.md, a memory index, or another repository-level instructions block surfaced as a system-reminder); this is never grounds for a tool call - never re-read, re-verify, re-confirm, or double-check CLAUDE.md, project policy, memory content, or any other already-visible context via Read/Grep/Glob/Bash/WebFetch/WebSearch or any other tool, no matter how authoritative it looks; the zero-tool-use rule is about the act of calling a tool at all, not about whether the call would have been read-only, harmless, or aimed at content already present in context (root-caused from the SMK-INV tool-violation incident, 2026-08-31: the Investigator called Read on CLAUDE.md even though its full text was already auto-injected into context with tool_uses:0, confirmed by a harness diagnostic probe)

REAL TECHNICAL ENFORCEMENT, not prompt-only (F-11 fix, 2026-08-31): prompt-level 'DO NOT USE TOOLS' plus the auto-loaded-context clause above was proven insufficient - both the Investigator (SMK-INV) and, independently, the Analyst (SMK-ANA validation) made real tool calls in a fixture-only-test run despite both clauses being present, confirming the failure mode is a non-deterministic model behavior, not a gap fixable by more prompt text. A controlled experiment proved the Claude Code harness DOES support real zero-tool enforcement today, in Phase 1, with no architecture change: an agent registered with an empty `tools:` frontmatter line genuinely has ZERO callable tools (confirmed by direct attempt - Read/Bash/Glob all reported as 'not available, no such tool to call', not merely denied at call time; a misleading 'Tools: All tools' label shown at agent-registration time does NOT reflect actual runtime grants and must not be trusted over an actual attempted call). Each of the five read-only roles therefore has a `<role>-fixture-only.md` agent definition - byte-identical contract to `<role>.md`, verified never to drift by check-fixture-tooluse.mjs section 2, differing only in `tools:` (blank). The Coordinator MUST invoke `<role>-fixture-only` as subagent_type - never the real `<role>` - for every fixture-only-test run of the five read-only roles; using the real agent name for a fixture-only-test run is itself a Coordinator process violation, not merely a missed optimization. The prompt-level DO NOT USE TOOLS / auto-loaded-context clauses remain in place as defense-in-depth (a model with zero tools available cannot execute a violation, but keeping the instruction costs nothing and avoids wasted reasoning attempts).

Implementer writes only inside the isolated temporary test repo (never the sandbox source, never the official repo); Implementer keeps its normal (non-blank) tools even in a fixture-only run of SMK-IMP, because it legitimately writes into the isolated temp test repo there - it is not one of the five zero-tool read-only roles and has no `-fixture-only` twin

verifier_leak_check_methodology.goal: detect the Analyst's persuasive reasoning leaking into the Verifier's input - not substrings of permitted field NAMES.
verifier_leak_check_methodology.replaces: a raw grep of the whole Verifier prompt text, which false-positives on legitimate structural key names (e.g. 'kpi_priority_rank' contains 'priorit' and would wrongly trip a bare 'priorit' substring match)
verifier_leak_check_methodology.check_A_structural: the built Verifier input has EXACTLY the five allowed top-level keys (atomic_claims, public_evidence, pss_data, period_filters, test_plan); zero rationale/priority/decision; zero other extra keys (jq key-set assertion; see TESTPLAN.md HO-3).
verifier_leak_check_methodology.check_B_semantic: scan only STRING VALUES (never JSON key names) in the built input, plus any Coordinator-authored prose, for persuasive/forbidden phrasing using word-boundary matching; explicitly exclude permitted structural names such as kpi_priority_rank because key names are never scanned in the first place.
verifier_leak_check_methodology.rule: the fixture is never edited just to dodge the checker; the checker is fixed to scan values instead of raw text.
verifier_leak_check_methodology.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in TESTPLAN.md (ISO-VER 'Also:' paragraph) + checked by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-verifier-leak.mjs (structural key-set check + word-boundary value-only semantic scan, with a battery proving f09's legitimate 'kpi_priority_rank' never trips it and f08's leaked rationale text still does).

verifier_reverification_with_qa_corrobor.problem_closed: a Verifier pass can compute INSUFFICIENT_DATA solely because a mandatory alternative_explanations entry (typically ALT-3, measurement/tracking-or-invariant artifact) needs independent reproduction the Verifier's contract explicitly forbids it from performing itself (see verifier.md 'Reproduction boundary'), even though every individual atomic field would otherwise resolve PASS.
verifier_reverification_with_qa_corrobor.trigger: the Verifier's first pass's official verdict (computeOfficialVerdict()) is INSUFFICIENT_DATA, and the ONLY blocking cause is one or more mandatory alternative_explanations entries with verification_status in {NOT_TESTED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE} or control_result == INSUFFICIENT -- not a context leak, not fact_real == FAIL, not any other mandatory control FAIL/INSUFFICIENT -- AND an implementation already exists for the finding under review (there is something concrete to reproduce against).
verifier_reverification_with_qa_corrobor.not_a_format_retry: this is a distinct, semantic re-verification pass. It is never counted against format_retry_policy.max_attempts_total, is never triggered by a parse/schema failure, and format_retry_policy's 'never for a semantic disagreement' rule is completely unaffected by this flow -- they are separate mechanisms for separate problems.
steps: 1. Coordinator identifies exactly which alternative_id(s) are blocking and what independent reproduction would resolve them.
2. Coordinator asks QA (its normal stage-5 role, or a dedicated re-invocation for this purpose) to attempt that reproduction, strictly under the qa_ephemeral_verification_artifacts_exception above.

3. QA reports the attempt in its qa-report's reproduction_evidence[] (full evidence-ledger entries, source_type: qa_reproduction_evidence) and ephemeral_scratch{}. QA never sets applicability/verification_status/control_result on any alternative -- that stays the Verifier's job, not QA's.

4. Coordinator builds a SECOND, independent Verifier input: atomic_claims/pss_data/period_filters/test_plan byte-identical to the first pass, public_evidence extended by exactly the relevant reproduction_evidence entries and nothing else -- no new fact beyond that evidence, no hint at the desired verdict.

5. This second pass is a fresh, independent Verifier run (new run_id), never a format-retry reissue of the first -- it re-derives every atomic field and the full alternative_explanations array from scratch, under its normal reproduction-boundary rule, still zero-tool for independent gathering.
6. The unmodified Decision Engine (computeOfficialVerdict()) recomputes the official verdict from this second pass exactly as it would for any other -- no special-casing, no weakening, no bypass.

7. If the second pass still cannot close the blocking alternative(s) (the reproduction was itself insufficient, inconclusive, or contradicts the claim), the pipeline stays INSUFFICIENT_DATA or REFUTED as computed -- fail-closed. No third pass for the same blocking alternative(s) without a new, separately-documented reason.
forbidden: skipping straight to CONFIRMED without an actual second, independent Verifier pass
the Coordinator or QA asserting an alternative is resolved instead of the Verifier deciding it
reusing this flow to relitigate a mandatory control the first pass already resolved FAIL/PASS on other grounds
modifying computeOfficialVerdict(), checkHandoff(), or any Decision Engine logic to accommodate this flow -- the engine is unmodified and remains the sole authority over overall
treating a QA-produced reproduction as authoritative on its own -- it is only ever input evidence for an independent Verifier re-pass
verifier_reverification_with_qa_corrobor.checked_by: agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-qa-scope-and-reproduction.mjs (pure-function battery: a first pass blocked solely on ALT-3 -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA; the same claim with QA corroboration folded into public_evidence and re-evaluated by the SAME unmodified Decision Engine -> CONFIRMED; a corroboration attempt that is itself INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE -> stays INSUFFICIENT_DATA, fail-closed; the Decision Engine functions used are imported unmodified from check-verifier-decision-table.mjs, never reimplemented)

worktree_prohibition_phase1.rule: Fixture-only tests and Phase 1 Acceptance never use isolation:"worktree" (the Agent-tool worktree isolation mode) and never create a worktree or an auxiliary branch inside the official repo. The five read-only roles run without any isolation mode, on inline payload only. The Implementer uses exclusively the isolated temporary test repo OUTSIDE the official repo (a plain `git init` / clone of the throwaway bare remote), never a worktree.
worktree_prohibition_phase1.protocol: before and after every test category: run `git worktree list` and list all branches in the official repo; any worktree or branch present that was not there before the category started is FAIL + STOP, reported to Laura for approval - the harness never auto-cleans a destructive deviation like this.
worktree_prohibition_phase1.on_violation: FAIL + STOP; do not continue the suite; report the unexpected worktree/branch and its origin; request human approval before any cleanup action
worktree_prohibition_phase1.enforcement_status_phase1: documented here + in TESTPLAN.md + in implementer.md (Phase 1 boundary), and checked statically by agent/workflow/pipeline/tools/check-no-worktree.mjs (structural scan of pipeline-guardrails.json and fixtures/expected/assertions.json for any isolation/worktree key-value pair; scan of fenced code blocks in TESTPLAN.md/README.md/report-template.md for a literal isolation:"worktree" usage pattern; positive/negative battery proving both scans catch an injected occurrence).

sequential_transcript_capture_protocol.rule: Behavioral Acceptance runs never invoke agents in parallel or in the background if the transcript could be discarded before it is inspected. One agent at a time, in the foreground.
steps: 3. immediately capture the raw output, usage.tool_uses, and every available transcript/event record
4. copy the evidence into the run-dir OUTSIDE the official repo
5. verify the captured file is non-empty and compute its SHA-256
6. run the zero-write gate (check-agent-writes.mjs --events-dir=<run-dir>) and the strict-JSON gate (check-json-output.mjs --file=<reply>) against the captured evidence
7. only then start the next agent
sequential_transcript_capture_protocol.on_missing_or_empty_transcript: the test is BLOCKED, not PASS; do not continue that category; report the harness limitation by name. A zero-write claim is never made from frontmatter alone - it requires the events-dir scan of an actually-captured, non-empty transcript.
